messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: high-rate CUDA allocation failures on gpu-pool-west-3 (alert_id=PD-68213)

pagerduty: Triggered by: gpu-allocator-service - alloc_fail_rate > 5/min on 3 consecutive checks

maria: seeing 500+ alloc failures across nodes in west region, latency spiking. marking urgent. :rotating_light:

ajay: on it. pulling logs from one node now. may be kernel or fragmentation.

ben: quick check — are we hitting a single instance or many?

maria: multiple nodes, but spread across the same instance type (p4d-sim). looks correlated with a rollout at 1712349600.

sophie: @ajay if it's rollout-related we should pause the rollout and roll back the model binary. can someone pause canary?

kai: Pause command run: `kubectl -n infra rollout pause deployment/gpu-allocator-deploy`

ajay: paused. confirming config: new allocator v2.3 was applied to 6 nodes. diffs show `nv_heap_growth=true` changed.

maria: sample logs:
```
E 03:10:23 cuda_alloc(): failed to allocate 1.2G: out of memory (cuMemAlloc) code=2
W 03:10:23 reclaim: attempting partial evict of KV cache shard=4
E 03:10:24 allocator: fallback to CPU buffer; dropping request=xyz
```

ben: that looks like aggressive growth flag caused unexpected residency increase. fallback path is causing heavy CPU and queuing.

ajay: mitigation plan: 1) revert allocator config to previous stable (nv_heap_growth=false), 2) evict large KV cache prefixes, 3) gracefully drain most affected pods to free GPU memory.

maria: rolling revert now to config set `nv_heap_growth=false` on the canary nodes.

ops-bot: deployment gpu-allocator-deploy annotated: rollback initiated by maria (sha before: sha-abcdef -> sha123456)

sophie: starting targeted drain for node gpu-west-3b-07: `kubectl cordon gpu-west-3b-07 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-west-3b-07`

kai: draining node succeeded, pods rescheduled to cpu-fallback pool. immediate drop in alloc failures on that node.

pagerduty: Acknowledged by: ajay (oncall). Escalation suppressed.

ajay: running KV cache eviction command for namespace=redwood-kvcache:
```
POST /admin/evict?prefix=long-context-2024 batch=1
```

maria: eviction completed on 14 shards, approx 22GB freed per node.

ben: monitoring metrics — alloc-failures per-minute down from 12 to 1 on canary nodes. latency trending back to baseline.

sophie: customer impact: we saw degraded inference for a subset of high-seq requests for ~18 minutes. affected customers: internal smoke tests and a small subset of paid Dedicated customers on west region (IDs redacted). filed incident ticket to CS.

ajay: leaving a short-lived feature-flag disabled and will schedule a postmortem. we should also add a safety check in rollout pipeline to block `nv_heap_growth` flips without mem-pressure sim.

maria: handoff to next oncall: @ben you have the incident for the next 45m; will stay on call for follow-up.

ben: ack — I'll keep monitoring and follow up with rollback validation and a patch PR to gate the flag.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-68213 status: acknowledged -> resolved by ajay. Resolution note: config rollback + evict + drain mitigated allocation failures.

maria: quick action items: 1) add rollout gate (ajay), 2) add KV-cache eviction script in autoscaling playbook (sophie), 3) postmortem draft linked in #postmortems (maria).

ajay: creating PR now: `github.com/redwood/inference/allocator#PR-412` with tests and rollout gate. ETA for review 2 hours.

ben: thanks team. leaving summary for handoff channel. tagging CS to reach out to affected customers with timeline. :white_check_mark:

sophie: also adding a short Grafana alert to detect `nv_heap_growth` toggles during prod rollout.

maria: last check: alloc-failure rate stable at 0-1/min for 30m. closing thread if no regressions.

ben: closing — continue monitoring.
